back: Mineral matter, organic matter (humus), water, air and living organisms.

front: Typical composition of a loam by volume
back: About 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% water, 25% air (varies with wetness).
Water held by a soil after saturation once gravitational water has drained away.
Soil water content at which plants wilt and do not recover.
Available water = field capacity − permanent wilting point.
Gravitational (drains away), capillary (available to plants), hygroscopic (held too tightly, unavailable).
Lime water turns milky beside fresh soil (respiration gives CO₂) but not beside heat-sterilised soil.
Useful: decomposers, Rhizobium, earthworms, mycorrhizae. Harmful: root-knot nematodes, cutworms, disease fungi and bacteria, denitrifiers.
